subject: Problem when using the functions "setMKLthreads" and "getMKLthreads"

messages.author: b6cc04db2c701a9f
messages.subject: Problem when using the functions "setMKLthreads" and "getMKLthreads"
parts:
Hello everybody,

I just installed Revolution R open and the Revobase package on a 4-cores pc. However, when the function "getMKLthreads" is called, it returns a value of 2 only. If I use the functions "setMKLthreads(4)" then the following message comes out:

Number of threads at maximum: no change has been made.

Thank you for your help,

AF

messages.author: 0eb5a09fd4de9e5e
messages.subject: Re: Problem when using the functions "setMKLthreads" and "getMKLthreads"
parts:
You don't supply enough information to diagnose accurately, but here is my guess:

You are running a machine with an Intel processer with hyperthreading (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyper-threading).  This means you have a CPU with 2 physical cores, each capable of hyperthreading, thus looking to the OS like 4 cores.

However, the MKL will only use the physical cores without hyperthreading.

For example, on my Intel Core I7 (4 cores with hyperthreading, thus 8 cores) I can only set the MKL threads to 4.

> library(parallel)

> detectCores()
[1] 8

> setMKLthreads(8)
Number of threads at maximum: no change has been made.

> getMKLthreads()
[1] 4


Regards

Andrie

messages.author: 0eb5a09fd4de9e5e
messages.subject: Re: Problem when using the functions "setMKLthreads" and "getMKLthreads"
parts:
Hi, Alberto

Using the logical processors would make almost no difference in computing speed, other than possibly slowing down the overall performance.

The reason is this:
  • Parallel processing requires overhead of communication between cores, thus the overall performance increase is lower than the available parallel units.  See  Amdahls's law http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amdahl%27s_law
  • Hyperthreading works by buffering input/output and then switching a physical core to different computation tasks
  • For a high performance compute problem, e.g. matrix algebra, the I/O overhead is low and the compute task is large.
  • Consequently using logical cores will only decrease performance (Amdahl's law)
The MKL already optimizes your available parallel computing resource.  This is why I would not expect Intel to make any change to this architecture.

(Somebody please prove me wrong.)

Regards

Andrie
